candidacy: NMDAR block (d-APV in probe form; clinical-class analogues memantine or Mg2+ are NOT tested in any WWOX system)
identity_and_active_moiety: D-AP5 competitive antagonist, GluN2A-D non-selective; memantine/Mg2+ would be different moieties and are not transferred
context: P13-17 mouse slice (bursting abolished, reversible); human organoid never tested
counter_evidence: (i) NMDAR dependence of bursting is not WWOX-specific; (ii) resting potential 5 mV depolarised (relieves Mg2+ block), so effect may be circumstantial; (iii) chronic NMDAR block in developing cortex is a known risk class (general knowledge, not sourced here); (iv) F04/F01 cards already carry this
decisive_missing_datum: fraction of NMDAR current to block to stop bursting, in a WT slice made to burst by a matched trigger (specificity), then Ca2+ event rate in WOREE organoids at the add-back timing
ex_vivo_utility: high (tool, reversible, same Ca2+ readout available)
systemic_requirements: not a drug (poor penetration); neonatal NMDAR-block risk; none assessed here
verdict: KEEP as probe arm in the discriminating experiment; no development claim

context: null pups: genotype-specific PTZ effect; spontaneous SWD never tested
counter_evidence: SWD in this model may not be thalamic absence type; PTZ-provoked is not spontaneous; floor of low-dose PTZ in controls untested alternative

systemic_requirements: approved paediatric drug but exposure and window (null dies ~P15) limit
verdict: KEEP as the same-readout test in mouse; does not address the human organoid readout

candidacy: chronic activity silencing (tetrodotoxin or chronic AP5) from week 10 to 16 as a probe, not a therapy
identity_and_active_moiety: TTX (Nav block) and D-AP5 as two independent silencers; moieties kept separate
action: remove firing without WWOX; asks whether CTIP2/SATB2 and the ion-channel programme are activity-dependent
context: WOREE and SCAR12 organoids with the RC1 timeline
hypothesised_benefit: if silencing alone does not raise CTIP2/SATB2, firing and layer identity are separable readouts (as SCAR12 suggests); if it does, a bypass of the layer-marker readout exists
counter_evidence: SCAR12 already shows firing high with layer markers normal (one allele, small n, by eye), predicting no effect; chronic silencing alters maturation in many systems (general knowledge)
decisive_missing_datum: CTIP2/SATB2 and event rate in the same silenced organoids, scored against WOREE-EGFP and WOREE-WWOX
verdict: ADOPT as arm of the discriminating experiment (restates the K01 step-0 activity-silenced arm; extends it to layer markers)

candidacy: BMP-pathway ligands for the layer-identity readout: eptotermin alfa (BMP-7) and dibotermin alfa (BMP-2)
identity_and_active_moiety: recombinant human BMP-7 (CHEMBL2108594) and BMP-2 (CHEMBL2109171); main target BMPR1A (contribution hops 1-3 to SATB2; path edges not audited)

counter_evidence: WWOX loss RAISES TGFb/BMP2 signalling in pancreatic cancer cells (36572673, title and abstract level only), i.e. BMP gain would push with the lesion in that context; no neural WWOX BMP datum; engine Z on two seeds is not evidence; recombinant protein
decisive_missing_datum: direction of BMP-SMAD activity (pSMAD1/5/8) in WOREE vs WT organoid neurons
verdict: DO NOT ADVANCE; listed as an engine output with its counter-evidence

candidacy: the add-back effect on firing is over-expression/WPRE gain-of-function, not recovery of WWOX function
identity_and_active_moiety: AAV9-hSynI-WWOX-2A-EGFP-WPRE in neurons that show no WWOX in untreated WT (Fig 6A i)

candidacy: non-WWOX anticonvulsant actions that merely lower firing (lithium, ethosuximide, d-APV) are symptomatic and unrelated to WWOX function

context: wild-type also affected (lithium); genotype-specific only for ethosuximide
counter_evidence: lithium suppresses in all three genotypes
decisive_missing_datum: reading a layer-marker, myelin and glia readout alongside firing
verdict: KEEP as the null reading every bypass must beat: a firing change alone is not recovery
